about.title: Thousand Oaks Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When someone dies because of another person's carelessness, the paperwork arrives before the grief has anywhere to go. Thousand Oaks recorded four traffic deaths in 2025 alongside 616 injury collisions, and each of those numbers stands for a household in Ventura County trying to make sense of what comes next. Some of these losses trace back to US-101, others to Thousand Oaks Boulevard, Hillcrest Drive, or Moorpark Road; many have nothing to do with a car at all. California treats wrongful death as a civil matter, separate from any criminal charges, and gives most families two years from the date of death to file. That window narrows considerably if a public agency is involved. Who may bring the claim is also defined by statute, starting with a spouse or domestic partner and children. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect Thousand Oaks families, free of charge, with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: What a Thousand Oaks Family Should Know Before Filing

items.title: Only certain relatives can file
items.desc: California gives first priority to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children, followed by specific dependents and heirs. An attorney can confirm who in your family has standing before anything is filed.

items.title: The clock is already running
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death. If a city, county, or state agency may share responsibility, the deadline to give notice is much shorter.

items.title: Losses go beyond the funeral bill
items.desc: Recoverable losses can include burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. These are civil remedies, independent of any criminal prosecution.

items.question: My spouse was killed in a crash on US-101 near Thousand Oaks. Does it matter that it was a freeway?
items.answer: It can. Freeways like the Ventura Freeway are maintained by the state, and if road conditions or design played any role, a government entity could be involved. Claims against public agencies in California carry a much shorter notice deadline than the standard two years, so speaking with an attorney early protects your options.

items.question: The driver is facing criminal charges in Ventura County. Do we have to wait for that case to end?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action with its own deadline, and it does not depend on a conviction. Many families pursue both at the same time, and an attorney can explain how evidence from the criminal matter may be useful in the civil case.

items.question: How does LawProactive help, and what does it cost?

Our service connects you with an independent attorney who takes wrongful death matters on contingency, meaning there is no attorney fee unless there is a recovery. The connection itself is free, and there is no obligation to move forward.
